key_insight: EHR representations mix patient physiology with care processes, and neither a single dataset nor cross-site outcome invariance alone can identify their separation.
clinical_relevance: Differences in model behavior across hospitals may reflect testing practices and patient mix rather than changes in underlying biology.
method: Formalized how physiology, test ordering, recorded values, representations, and clinical environments interact.
Derived identification limits for separating laboratory-value and ordering information.
Constructed observationally equivalent models and established conditions under which measured tests restore identification.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results and a worked example showing a 9.6-percentage-point cross-site gap despite an unchanged biological mechanism, not clinical validation.
watch_item: Report cross-site analyses as tests of a stated joint hypothesis; identifying biological invariance requires additional measurement and modeling assumptions.
paper_title: The Dark Matter of Clinical Data: An Identification Limit on Disentangling Physiology from Care Process in electronic health records
